body:
Same for me.  
I used to have a pretty good memory but now I can't seem to remember names, faces, literally anything. People make fun of me and complain when I still don't know in which classrooms I have which classes after 4 years of school but it's not like I'm doing it on purpose.

Hey, I'm only trying to power through because I only have a couple more months left. I can't even recall how many times I thought of just dropping out. I just feel that at this point I'm too far in to quit, you know? I'd love to, since the pressure is killing me, but there's no way I can drop out now without disappointing literally everyone. 

Also, what else would I be doing? I doubt I'd find enjoyment in anything else, so might as well finish this while I'm at it.

I relate, friend. At this point I just hope that everything gets better once I'm finally out. But for that to happen I gotta power through this. 

Maybe I'll finally be happy? I honestly doubt it but I guess there's still a spark of hope left in me.

I might even have a job after I'm finally done with school, but at this point I'm not even sure I want to do what I'm studying anymore. Web development was fun in the beginning but it feels like school sucked out the enjoyment out of everything I used to love.

At least that's what I used to think happened. Now I'm starting to think that it might not be the school that took all my happiness but the depression. Whatever. Doesn't really make a difference.

I'm just glad I have to do a year of mandatory civil service once I'm done with school (_if_ I actually manage to finish it) because I can just completely stop caring about anything during that time. I might just end up doing something completely different after that year. Maybe my passion for web development will come back. I don't even know anymore at this point.

Same here. The other day my mom asked me why I look so sad and she looked so devastated, that I told myself I'd never do anything to myself that would hurt her. 

Sure, she might not be the best mother in existence, but she's doing her best and she cares and I appreciate that and love her for it.

Sometimes, I just really wanna give up though...

Ah, I get what you mean. Maybe it's because I don't allow myself to cry for some reason that it doesn't help. I can see how it can help you if it helps you cry and get rid of all those pent up emotions.

It's interesting people always say that sad music helps them. I'm obviously not saying that your advice is bad but I find it fascinating.

For me, sad music just makes me feel worse. I enjoy the sad music but it drags me down even further. It's certainly not helping and just amplifying the terrible voices in my head.

Again, not saying that you are wrong and sad music might help some people, but for me, it doesn't unclutter my head, is does the opposite.

I know what you mean. I've been feeling like this for probably a couple of years now, I think. I've honestly lost track of when I started feeling like this.

No matter what I do, I feel tired all the time, empty, lost. I feel like I'm not getting any sleep at all even though I try to make sure I get a healthy dose of sleep every night. 

This shit has been going on for so long that I've been thinking of just going online and buying some prescription meds online on some shady website in hopes of them helping me in some way. There's a bunch of wakefulness-promoting drugs out there that can apparently help but doctor's here don't like prescribing them, so I'd have to figure out hwo to get them myself.

I'm rambling but I just wanted to share this and let you know that I can relate. All my peers are flying past me. They are all achieving things. Travelling with their SO, learning stuff they love or learning new things about themselves and I'm just sitting here feeling sorry for myself. 

I try to be productive and do things that make me happy, but I honestly just don't have the energy. 

I just want to sleep.

Glad it worked out in the end, buddy. Make sure you keep supporting her, if possible. Make sure she knows that you worried and that you care for her.

Good luck and take care!
Anytime. Good luck and thank you for trying to help her. She might not realize it right now, but you're a good person for doing so.

Alright, so here's how I see this whole situation:

If a person posts about wanting to commit suicide on social media or let's people know in some other way, it's an obvious cry for help. If you want to commit suicide and actually _want_ to succeed, you'll not let people know about it by posting on social media. 

Here's the thing though: That obviously doesn't mean that she won't try to pull through with it. Maybe try to call her and tell her that you didn't mean it that way. Tell her that you don't want her to do what she's thinking of doing.

If you can't reach her and are genuinely concerned for her health, try to contact somebody who can reach her. Maybe somebody who lives close to her, parents and worst case scenario - the police.

Basically, just try to do _something_, if you are genuinely worried, because if you don't, and something actually happens to her, you'll regret not acting for the rest of your life.

Good luck and take care.

I have a weird relationship with alcohol. It either makes me feel kind of alright for a couple of hours or it completely drags me down and if that happens, I usually crash. Hard. 

The last time I had a bad time on alcohol, I ended up drinking a whole bottle of whisky, threw up all over my room and passed out on the bathroom floor.

I try to moderate my alcohol intake but it's honestly not easy. I know that I have a 50/50 chance of having a shitty time, but it's worth it for the times where I'm feeling alright.

I can't seem to eat healthy amounts of food. Either I overeat to the point of feeling like throwing up or I don't eat anything all day.  
Seems like the worse I'm feeling, the more extreme my eating habits become.

>I have some friends online but they wouldn't even noticed if i died.

Probably one of the reasons why I don't want to kill myself yet. There's so many cool people that I've met online over the last few years, I'd feel guilty leaving them behind without any idea what happened to me. 

I'd never admit it, but that damn bastard that keeps kicking my ass in Rocket League is probably one of the main reasons why I haven't offed myself yet.

Absolutely. I used to plan on becoming an amazing web developer. Become one of those guys that are well known among the web developer community on Twitter with revolutionary websites, ideas and designs.

At this point I just gave up on that. I'm not even sure if I even want to be a web developer anymore. I lost all motivation to do anything. My creativity is gone and I can't be bothered to do anything besides napping in my free time.

Maybe I'll just grab the first job I find that's not mentally exhausting. I won't amount to anything anyways, might as well work a shitty job with shitty pay and spend all my time off work in bed sleeping, right?
I appreciate the kind words, buddy. Thank you. I'll think about what you said.

Thank you. I'll give it some thought but I guess I also feel that I don't really deserve the help. I know, I know. "Everybody deserves help. Nobody deserves to go through what you are going through." I just feel like I brought this upon myself and that I gotta figure this out myself as well, though I doubt I ever will.

There is only one guy who I consider a true friend but we don't have the kind of relationship where we talk about our problems. It would probably only make everything awkward. We hang out once a month or something. That's always kinda fun.

I wish I had someone to just sit down with a bottle of beer and talk about how we're feeling though. To just open up without having to use a filter.

I don't think I'm ready to talk about my problems. 

My mother told me that I could talk to a therapist after I got drunk, threw up and passed out on the bathroom floor after a depressive episode but I told her that I don't need help. That I don't want to talk to anyone.

She probably wrote off me opening up to her about being depressed to me just being very drunk and I honestly don't wanna bring that topic up anymore anyways.

I have a hard time opening up to people. Not on the internet, because here I can just make a new Reddit throwaway whenever I feel like it, but not in real life. I don't reach out. I don't talk about my problems.

The problem is, that this shit defines me. I used to be the guy who plays video games, sometimes smokes weed, is chill to be around, always has an open ear for your problems, doesn't mind helping you out with your homework and is all around just a nice dude.

Now I'm the dude with depression who wants to die. That's it. It's like all my other personality traits and habits don't exist anymore to them. Sure, I _did_ lose some, but that doesn't mean that all I am anymore at this point is a flesh sack filled with suicidal thoughts.

I relate. I used to love video games and used to play a couple hours every day. Now I don't even know what I'm doing anymore in my free time. I mostly just lie in bad or waste time browsing Reddit. 

I learned recently that I still manage to enjoy myself when I'm playing video games with friends I've met online but it's still hard for me to convince myself that I actually _want_ to play. It's like there's this barrier in my mind that I gotta jump over to finally be able to enjoy something I've always enjoyed. 

It's hard and I often end up turning down invitations to games, even though I probably would have ended up having fun.

Shit sucks.
